attributes.morphology: irregularly shaped silicides randomly distribute on continuous Nbss

evidence.quote: The 0Mo-0Zr alloy contains two different crystal structures of 5–3 silicides, α(Nb,X)5Si3 (tetragonal, D8l structure) ("X" represents the alloying elements which substitute for Nb in the lattices) and γ(Nb,X)5Si3 (hexagonal, D88 structure)

attributes.morphology: eutectic structure with irregularly shaped silicides

evidence.quote: It can be determined that the silicides with dark contrast are γ(Nb,X)5Si3, since their compositions (Table 1) and morphologies (Fig. 2) are similar to the silicides in the other three alloys that only contain γ(Nb,X)5Si3.
It is observed that all alloys consist of Nbss and 5–3 silicides.

while the other three alloys only possess γ(Nb,X)5Si3, suggesting that both single and composite additions of Mo and Zr suppress the formation of α(Nb,X)5Si3 phase whilst promote the formation of γ(Nb,X)5Si3 phase.

attributes.morphology: cellular or dendritic Nbss phases form in the outer part of eutectics

evidence.quote: After alloying with 5 at% Mo in the alloys, the eutectic in 5Mo-0Zr alloy exhibits a fine structure with petal-like morphology, and the cellular or dendritic Nbss phases form in the outer part of eutectics

A region with similar morphology and composition was also observed and confirmed as three-phase eutectic consisting of Cr2Nb, Nbss and γ(Nb,X)5Si3 by the micro-area XRD analysis in our previous work [8].
Quantitative metallographic analysis shows that the amount of primary γ(Nb,X)5Si3 blocks in 0Mo-4Zr alloy is ~16.1% (Fig. 3, area fraction)
However, in the Zr-containing alloys (0Mo-4Zr and 5Mo-4Zr alloys), another different eutectic containing lamellar Nbss has formed, as indicated by the arrows in Fig. 2c and d.
while that of 5Mo-4Zr alloy decreases to ~12.8% (Fig. 3, area fraction)
However, in the Zr-containing alloys (0Mo-4Zr and 5Mo-4Zr alloys), another different eutectic containing lamellar Nbss has formed, as indicated by the arrows in Fig. 2c and d.
the microhardness of γ(Nb,X)5Si3 and Nbss in 0Mo-0Zr alloy is ~1005 and ~590 Hv, respectively.
the microhardness of γ(Nb,X)5Si3 and Nbss in 0Mo-0Zr alloy is ~1005 and ~590 Hv, respectively.
After single addition of Mo in the alloys, the microhardness of Nbss and γ(Nb,X)5Si3 increases to ~678 Hv and ~1054 Hv, respectively.
After single addition of Mo in the alloys, the microhardness of Nbss and γ(Nb,X)5Si3 increases to ~678 Hv and ~1054 Hv, respectively.
After single addition of Zr in the alloys, the microhardness of γ(Nb,X)5Si3 in 0Mo-4Zr alloy rises to ~1198 Hv and is higher than that in 5Mo-0Zr alloy.
Thus, the microhardness of Nbss in 0Mo-4Zr alloy is close to that in 0Mo-0Zr alloy.

conditions.test_method: three-point bend test, single edge notched bending specimen

evidence.quote: the average KQ value of 0Mo-0Zr alloy is ~10.7 MPa m1/2.

conditions.test_method: three-point bend test, single edge notched bending specimen

evidence.quote: After alloying with Mo, the 5Mo-0Zr alloy’s KQ value decreases to ~8.1 MPa m1/2.

conditions.test_method: three-point bend test, single edge notched bending specimen

evidence.quote: While after adding Zr alone to the alloys, the KQ value of 0Mo-4Zr alloy increases to ~13.8 MPa m1/2, which is the highest value in the four alloys.

conditions.test_method: three-point bend test, single edge notched bending specimen

evidence.quote: the further addition of Mo in the alloys deteriorates the room temperature fracture toughness again, since the KQ value of 5Mo-4Zr alloy decreases to ~9.2 MPa m1/2, compared with 0Mo-4Zr alloy.

the large amount of Mo dissolved in Nbss and slight solution of Mo in silicides, playing a role of solid solution strengthening, are responsible for the increased microhardness of phases in 5Mo-0Zr alloy.
the lattice distortion caused by the substitution of Nb with Zr in γ(Nb,X)5Si3 is higher than that caused by the substitution of Nb with Mo

Both the γ(Nb,X)5Si3 and Nbss in 5Mo-4Zr alloy show the highest microhardness in the four alloys, which is naturally attributed to the synergetic effects of solid solution strengthening of Zr and Mo in phases.
